body.statement: For every \(0<\rho<1\), the limit defining \(\Gamma_{\rho,w}(\mu)\) exists and equals the finite branch minimum \[\Gamma_{\rho,w}(\mu)=\min\left\{Q_h^{\mathrm E}(\rho,\mu),\ \min_{e\ne h}\min_{j\ne e,h}Q_{e,j}^{\mathrm T}(\rho,\mu)\right\}.\] Each infimum over a closed branch polyhedron equals the infimum over its strict-interior error event, and replacing ideal proportions by the largest-remainder counts \(N_T\) leaves this limit unchanged.
body.justification: Exact equality, rather than a one-sided concentration exponent, is necessary for an optimality frontier.
body.gap: Imbens, Qin, and Wager are the closest same-design comparator: under a common Gaussian variance, their batched arm-elimination result gives sufficient conditions for strict large-deviation dominance over uniform allocation, but it does not establish a heteroskedastic exact branch formula. The first changed steps are the weighted Gaussian contraction of each elimination branch and exact equality for the coupled terminal branches that reuse first-batch observations, including strict-interior attainment and rounding invariance.
body.consumer: The equality gives ranking-and-selection software a finite list of convex programs that exactly diagnose whether elimination or final comparison drives asymptotic error.
